hints.title: Sliding Window Maximum Extension
hints.text: Optimal subsequence sum ending at index i depends on the maximum subsequence sum ending at an index j within distance k.

hints.title: Decreasing Deque Invariant
hints.text: A double-ended buffer maintaining indices with decreasing dp values allows O(1) retrieval of the maximum value within the preceding k positions.

hints.title: Monotonic Buffer Sliding Transition Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a double-ended buffer storing index pairs. For each number at index i, pop front elements with index smaller than i - k. Set dp[i] = nums[i] + max(0, buffer[0].val). Evict elements from back smaller than dp[i], append (dp[i], i), and track the global maximum.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input length or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(K) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all k predecessor states for each element takes O(N * K), which is too slow when N and K are 100,000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A monotonic double-ended queue maintains the sliding maximum in O(1) amortized time per element and O(K) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize dynamic programming with sliding window maximum optimization using a monotonic deque.
